Summary: MCIS, AISM Ubuntu VM requires reboot to enable VLAN20
Description: The Ubuntu version of the AISM VM is setup with vlan201 as default. When MICS is activated, VLAN201 is removed from the network interface file, and VLAN20 is added. But the change is not automatically applied. To get it working, it's required to manually reboot the AISM VM to get CrewHub service working. The Value added services projects do not have any tasks for doing this, and in my opinion, adding a task for doing a reboot is not the way to go when we want processes to be automated as much as possible. I assume there is a script or playbook pulling config from shore. Wouldn't it be able to detect interface changes and reboot the service if any changes are detected?

It explicitly *descoped the c5921* ("Cisco IOS, different mechanism"). This ticket covers the c5921, which has an *analogous latent exposure* — and was in fact the variant seen on customer vessels in DORA-6751. h4. Correction to the original scoping note The c5921 is not a bare Cisco-IOS appliance. It is a KVM guest running a *CentOS/RHEL-family Linux* (uses {{/etc/sysconfig/network-scripts/ifcfg-*}}) that hosts the Cisco ESR software router as a userspace process. Found while working on the Alpine 3.23 promotion (DORA-6818, PR on branch DORA-6818). *Fix* Add {{set -e}} to the top of the test script so any failing test fails the job, then fix any tests this exposes. *Services* || Service || Status || | fleet_edge_updater | Affected (2 hidden failures).
